1 · Collapse the TLG namespace modules onto the spec seam

Strong in-process

src/fleet/tlg/{ae,lb,ds,eg,dm,cm,mh,ex,vs}_namespace.py · src/fleet/tlg/_ard.py · _specs.py · _registry.py

Before — shallow

⋮

21 dispatch sites · 8 distinct kwarg sets · the amber interface bar is nearly the whole module.

After — deep
mh
spec
vs
spec
ex · cm · ae …
spec
summarize_ard · _ard.py
summarize_ard(df, spec, *, groupby, adsl)
The 14-argument contract stops being restated 21 times. Prefilters (fill_uncoded, the ABLFL guard) become spec fields instead of method bodies.
Problem

24 public methods over 9 modules and 2,863 lines forward 13.6 keyword arguments each into one engine, in only 8 distinct shapes.

Solution

The spec already holds every one of those arguments. Pass the spec, not its fields; each method names its spec class and hands over groupby and adsl.

Deletion test

Delete mh_namespace.py: the SOC→PT row definition concentrates into _specs.py. Concentrates.

Evidence — mh_namespace.py L63-81 
spec = spec or MHSummarySpec()

spec.validate_dataframe(self._df, group_col=group_col)
return summarize_ard(
    fill_uncoded(self._df, ["MHBODSYS", "MHDECOD"]),
    rows=spec.rows,          stats=spec.statistics,
    context="t_mh_summary",  group_col=group_col,
    pools=spec.pools,        column_order=spec.column_order,
    adsl=adsl,               adsl_filter=spec.adsl_filter,
    dataset_filter=spec.dataset_filter,
    header_rows=spec.header_rows,  nested=True,
    value_col=spec.value_col,      label_col=spec.label_col,
    decimals=spec.decimals,
)
  • ▸ interface: 14 kwargs → 3
  • ▸ locality: engine contract in one module
  • ▸ new template: one spec + one registry entry
  • ▸ prefilters stop hiding in method bodies

2 · A study-run module behind fleet run

Strong ports & adapters

src/fleet/cli.py L763-900 (_load_run_input · _compose_run_frame · _run_run) · src/fleet/mcp_server.py L215

Before — the algorithm is inside a command handler

Problem

The only implementation of “execute a study” — read both defines, compose each dataset’s inputs, left-join the declared ADSL columns, carry built frames forward, write — is reachable only through an argparse.Namespace. Fleet’s philosophy is that the Python surface is the product; this algorithm is not on it.

Solution

Lift it into a module that takes a StudyContext and yields per-dataset results. cli.py keeps the printing and the exit codes and nothing else.

Touches ADR-0001

ADR-0001 leaves mcp_server.py alone because it reaches into fleet.cli. It does not contradict this candidate — it names the missing module that would let that reach stop. No re-litigation needed.

Evidence — the leak is already live 
# src/fleet/mcp_server.py:215
from fleet.cli import _GROUPBY_CANDIDATES

# src/fleet/cli.py:880 — the whole study-run algorithm
frame = _compose_run_frame(ctx, ds, built)
ns = frame.sdtm if standard == "sdtm" else frame.adam
result = (
    ns.from_spec(path, dataset=name, strict=args.strict)
    .select(spec=path, dataset=name)
    .to_frame()
)
built[name] = result
  • ▸ leverage: one interface, three adapters
  • ▸ the interface becomes the test surface
  • ▸ mcp_server stops importing cli internals
  • ▸ notebook users can run a study
  • ▸ 1,078 lines of command bodies start shrinking

3 · Two problems wearing one costume: the therapeutic-area surface

Speculative needs grilling

src/fleet/adam/{onco,ophtha,peds,vaccine,metabolic,neuro}_namespace.py · core/_verb_mixin.py L1006 verbs() · tools/migrate.py L58

The arithmetic that separates the two problems
today
45 completions
4 are metabolic
delete the 4 weak verbs
the shared verbs are what fill the list, and they are load-bearing
worse
41 completions
0 are metabolic
Problem A — discovery

41 inherited verbs drown 4 domain verbs. Cannot be fixed by deleting anything: the chain needs .derivation(), .pin(), .to_frame() to still be there after a TA verb.

Dead end: overriding __dir__ won’t help — Pylance builds completions statically and never calls it at runtime.

Live option: verbs() already exists as a discovery module returning a frame of verb + summary, and already filters through _VERBS_EXCLUDE. The open question is whether discovery is supposed to happen in autocomplete at all.

Problem B — admission

No stated bar for what earns a verb. The test: if I delete this, does a user get the wrong answer, or just type more?

metabolic.waist_hip_ratio → waist / hip, rounded. Types more. Didn’t earn it.
vaccine.seroconversion_flag → the 4.0 is the WHO threshold, the != 0 is a divide-by-zero trap. Wrong answer. Earned it.
Precedent — this has been done before 
# src/fleet/tools/migrate.py:58
VERB_RENAMES = {
    "assign_no_ct": "assign",   "assign_ct": "assign",
    "hardcode_no_ct": "assign", "hardcode_ct": "assign",
    "dataset_level": "assign",  "assigned": "assign",
    "if_then_else": "case_when",
    "condderivation": "case_when",
    "lookup": "merge",
}

Six verbs became assign, and a libcst codemod rewrote users’ pipelines. “You can’t remove a verb in a regulated industry” already has an answer in this repo.

Proposal — three parts, only one is cheap
  1. Write the admission bar down. Applies forwards only. Costs nothing, stops the surface growing.
  2. Decide what verbs() is for. If it’s the discovery seam, make it namespace-aware and point the docs at it. If not, interface width is a constraint you accept.
  3. Leave existing verbs alone. Revisit under the migrate precedent only if the surface keeps growing.
Confirmed non-problem

_sub_namespace passes _lazy through unchanged and copies pins, pin lineage, variable lineage, pending FK checks and domain. The property hop does not materialise and drops no state.

4 · Derive spec parameters from the verb signature

Worth exploring in-process

src/fleet/core/spec_registry.py · adam/models.py · sdtm/models.py · define_xml/spec_generator.py · tests/unit/test_spec_parity.py

Before — one verb, five files
adam/namespace.py def chg(…, aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
core/spec_registry.py Param("aval", str, default="AVAL")
adam/models.py CHG = "chg"
tests/test_spec_parity.py Case(…)
define_spec_schema.json regenerated

46 entries · 827 lines · red bands restate what the signature already declares.

After — the signature is the declaration
adam/namespace.py
def chg(self, target, *, aval: str = "AVAL", base: str = "BASE")
name · type · default · required-ness — read once via inspect.signature
spec_registry.py define_template · kwarg · convert · alias
enum · schema · introspect derived

The registry declares only what a signature cannot say.

Problem

46 hand-kept registry entries restate parameter names, types and defaults that the verb signature already declares. The parity test catches a missing verb or a stale enum; it does not compare the parameter tables, so a renamed keyword or a changed default passes green.

The bug this allows

Change base="BASE" to something else in the method and forget the registry: the Python form and the define.yaml form of the same derivation now produce different numbers, and the Define-XML you filed describes neither.

Respects ADR-0001

fleet.introspect stays the surface and its frozen DTOs stay the contract. This changes only where the registry gets its facts — precisely the freedom ADR-0001 bought. Guardrails: the AST sweep in test_introspect.py and test_spec_parity.py.

Evidence — the same four facts, twice 
# core/spec_registry.py:1316
spec_algorithm(
    "chg", standard="adam", verb="chg",
    params=(
        Param("aval", annotation=str, default="AVAL"),
        Param("base", annotation=str, default="BASE"),
    ),
    description="Change from baseline (AVAL - BASE).",
    define_template="Change from baseline: {aval} - {base}.",
)

# adam/namespace.py:200 — the thing that actually runs
def chg(self, target: str, *, aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE") -> AdamNamespace: ...
$ inspect.signature(AdamNamespace.chg)
name='aval' annotation='str' default='AVAL' required=False
name='base' annotation='str' default='BASE' required=False
$ spec_registry.get_algorithm("adam", "chg")

name='base' annotation='str' default='BASE' required=False
  • ▸ drift becomes impossible, not tested-for
  • ▸ 5 of Param’s 10 fields become derived
  • ▸ locality: one source for parameter facts

5 · One module owns how Fleet phrases a problem

Worth exploring in-process

src/fleet/core/exceptions.py · _verb_mixin.py (37 raises) · _flag_mixin.py (11) · _pin_mixin.py (10) · adam/namespace.py (10) · cli.py

Before — 81 raise sites, each phrasing its own
"no dataset paths given and no study_config.yaml found…"
"no study_config.yaml found in the current directory or any parent…"
"no study_config.yaml found in the current directory or any parent…"
— cli.py, three commands, three phrasings
After — the phrasing concentrates

_validate_chain_exprs already produces the right shape — verb, target, offending column, “Did you mean…”, available columns, truncated at 25. That shape is hard-coded inside one method instead of being the module every raise site calls.

Problem

Message quality is a property of whoever wrote the raise. The good shape exists in exactly one method; ~70 other sites improvise, and the CLI says “config not found” three different ways.

Solution

A module that owns the phrasing — verb, target, what went wrong, what was available, the suggestion, the truncation. Raise sites supply facts, not prose.

Deletion test

Delete it and the difflib suggestion, the column listing and the 25-column truncation reappear at every site that wants them. Concentrates.

Sequencing constraint

This edits raise sites in the same files candidates 1, 2 and 4 rewrite. Do it early — so new code uses problem() from birth — or last. Not in the middle.

Top recommendation

2 · A study-run module behind fleet run

Fleet’s premise is that a clinical derivation is Python you can read, chain and test. Running a whole study is the one derivation that isn’t: it exists only inside a command handler, which is why mcp_server.py already imports a private name out of cli.py and why a notebook user has to shell out. It is also the smallest of the five: the algorithm is already written and already correct — it just has the wrong interface. One module, three adapters, and the tests stop needing a filesystem.

Suggested order

#2 (smallest, sets the “move the algorithm, keep the surface” precedent) → #5 (small, and everything after inherits the phrasing) → #1 (biggest mass, highest churn) → #4 (correctness payoff). #3 is a grilling track, not a build: its likely output is an ADR.
